note:
External reference geometry for blind benchmarks. Nothing here is committed: these are third-party artifacts, and AGENTS.md forbids putting them in this repository. ARCHITECTURE.md 16.6 is the rule they follow instead. `tools/corpus.py` fetches them and verifies every digest.

QUESTION MATERIAL LIVES IN `request`, AND THE RULE ABOUT IT IS NOT ABOUT DIGITS. A request is meant to be full of measurements -- somebody takes calipers to the extrusion slot, the panel, the rail. What it may not carry is a measurement of the reference part ITSELF, because that is what a blind reconstruction has to produce and what the scorer compares.

Two mechanisms enforce it, and the second exists because the first cannot work alone. (1) Every requirement must name a declared counterpart: its leading token has to appear in this entry's `counterparts`, so `extrusion_slot_opening` and `panel_stock` are admissible and `girth` and `overall_height` are not. That is an allowlist; two earlier designs used denylists -- a regex, then a no-digit rule with exemptions -- and reviews walked through them twelve, nineteen and about eighty times. (2) Every number anywhere in the question is compared against the reference's actual extents and volume, and a coincidence is refused.

The second check is not theoretical. This file previously stated `extrusion_series: "2020"` for a part whose x-extent is exactly 20.0 mm -- a correctly named counterpart handing over one of the three answers, which no wording rule could ever catch. The deck support states the profile again and *declares* what that gives away; see the disclosure paragraph below. The rail guide does not: its y-extent is 20.5 and a 2020 profile means a 20 mm face, so stating the profile there would have handed over a number that makes the axis wrong rather than right.

Provenance is STATED throughout, and that is deliberate. These numbers were read off Voron 2's published hardware; nobody in this repository has calipers or the parts. An earlier version claimed MEASURED with sources like 'calipers across the slot mouth', which was a stronger claim than the method supports. MEASURED stays in the permitted set because a real requester produces it -- this corpus simply does not.

Each entry states a `build_envelope_mm`: the space the part has to live in. `design-tool run` refuses to guess `envelope_mm` when geometry is authored, so a blind request must state one -- and it must be a constraint the requester has rather than the reference's own size with slack added, which would be the answer with a margin on it. These are deliberately generous and identical across entries, and they go through the same coincidence check as every other number.

The first blind run found a leak no rule was looking for. Every requirement's `source` read 'Voron 2 published hardware', and the purpose said 'deck panel' -- so a designer with any Voron familiarity was told the ecosystem, the part class and the hardware standard, which fixes the topology by recall rather than by derivation. The designer reported it unprompted. Sources are non-identifying now.

An entry may declare a `discloses` list: which of the reference's own measurements the question gives away, and why. That is a cost, not a convenience -- a disclosed axis is reported by the score as given rather than reconstructed, so every row here narrows what the benchmark establishes. It exists because for some parts the interface dimension and the answer dimension are the same number (docs/defects.md D30), and refusing the coincidence refuses the information a designer needs to derive anything. Undeclared coincidences are still refused. Unlike the exemption list this resembles, a disclosure names one measurement of one reference and says why, so a reviewer reading the diff sees exactly which axis stopped being a question.

voron2.why: Real functional printed parts designed around standard hardware -- M3 fasteners, aluminium extrusion, MGN9 linear rails, GT2 belts. That matters for a blind benchmark: the question can state what the part has to interface with, with the numbers a person would measure, without stating the part's own geometry. This field is not question material and is never handed to a generator.

request.purpose: Holds a flat panel down against an aluminium extrusion so the panel cannot lift. It bolts into the extrusion's slot and traps the panel edge under a lip.

requirements.name: extrusion_slot_opening
requirements.note: the T-slot a fastener drops into

discloses.why: this part bolts flat against the extrusion face, so the face width is also the part's width. Stating the profile is what lets a designer derive anything at all, and it gives away one of the three axes. The score reports that axis as given rather than reconstructed. docs/defects.md D30.

request.purpose: Holds a linear rail straight and true against an extrusion while it is bolted down. A jig: it registers the rail against the extrusion face so the rail cannot wander during assembly.

requirements.name: extrusion_slot_opening
requirements.note: the slot the rail is bolted through

request.purpose: Retains a flat panel inside the slot of an extrusion. It clips in without a fastener and holds the panel against the frame.

requirements.name: extrusion_slot_opening
requirements.note: the T-slot a fastener drops into

request.purpose: Clamps the cut end of a toothed belt so it cannot pull through under tension. The belt teeth mesh against a toothed face inside the clamp and a fastener draws the two halves together.
